deep.reconstruction:
The page holds three separate research notes. None contains a derivation; there are no computations on the page.

(1) Suggested doctoral topic: the three-body problem. The plan is to compile and sift the literature, criticise the results obtained so far and the viewpoints applied, point to further questions, and attack the problems. This is a supervision/programme note, with no mathematics.

(2) Programmatic remark against Weierstrass. Hilbert reports Weierstrass's view that the order (degree) of an integral rational function in homogeneous variables is too insignificant to found theories on. Hilbert says the opposite: the order is 'das einzig Tiefe' (the only deep thing). However, at least in domains of more than two variables, one must not cling to a single order. One must consider all relevant systems of order numbers. Doing so leads necessarily to the genus p, 'but one obtains more and deeper things'.

Modern reading (my interpretation, not on the page): for a homogeneous ideal or module, consider the whole sequence of numbers attached to every degree m, e.g. the number of linearly independent forms of degree m satisfying the defining conditions. This is the Hilbert (characteristic) function H(m). Hilbert later showed, in 'Über die Theorie der algebraischen Formen' (Math. Ann. 36, 1890), that H(m) is eventually a polynomial. Its coefficients carry the degree and, through the constant term, the (arithmetic) genus.

Illustration (mine, not on the page): for a plane curve of degree d, the forms of degree m modulo the curve's equation have dimension
H(m) = C(m+2,2) - C(m-d+2,2) = d*m - d(d-3)/2 for m >= d-2.
The constant term equals 1-p, with p = (d-1)(d-2)/2. So the genus is recovered from the 'system of order numbers', exactly as the note asserts.

(3) Start of a problem, continued on the next page. Hilbert writes 'Alle [ganz-, crossed out] rationalen Funktionen u = phi(x,y,z,...), v = psi(x,y,z,...), ...', which continues overleaf as '... bestimmen, welche ganze Funktionen von x,y,z,... sind'. The task is to determine all systems of rational functions u, v, ... of x, y, z, ... that are integral (polynomial) functions, presumably with an implicit condition. The most plausible reading, given 'ein-eindeutige Transformationen' a few lines later on the next page, is about rational or polynomial transformations and their inverses. That reading is uncertain. The problem is only stated, not worked.
